evidence: Sen. Vit. Beat. 23: domūs (sc. scrūtātiō), the searching of a house (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A searching, a search: Seneca has it of a house searched (Lewis & Short: post-Augustan and very rare), from scrūtārī, to search thoroughly. Its use for the check at an airport is our application: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no term for it, and Levi–Bini give īnspectiō for a check in general (p. 19).

phrases.latin: Ad scrūtātiōnem igitur ventum est, ubi custōdēs, nē quis rem perīculōsam in āëroplanum īnferat, omnium sarcinās excutiunt.
phrases.english: So they came to the security check, where the officers search everyone’s bags so that nobody takes anything dangerous onto the plane.

phrases.latin: Custōdēs sarcinās nostrās nunc excutient; nihil est quod timeās.
phrases.english: The officers are going to search our bags now; there’s nothing to be afraid of.
Once we’re through security, we’ll go to the gate.
